items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: He was a very young man. And I remember he set his drum up once for me.

ctx.x: He was in his late 30s when he died. Wasn't very old at all. No he was not.

He was a very young man. And I remember he set his drum up once for me. That's one of the things I can never forget that he set the drums up but I was very young. There's not too much I could do. And after he died well I still didn't lose interest because it must have been in me. Because my uncles all they were drummers. The whole family of the brothers was five of them drummers.
All five? That's right. What were their names? I remember the name Clay Giles.

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: Oh yeah, because my father was the youngest and they had about three of them, older than my daddy

ctx.x: Was he much older than your father?
Oh yeah, because my father was the youngest and they had about three of them, older than my daddy and he was the oldest. That's right.
Who did Oliver Jones or Olivier, I want to know about that?
